trigger: Waterborne emergency, such as a failure or significant interruption in key water treatment processes (for example unsafe chemical feed or loss of disinfection reaching the distribution system), or another situation the primacy agency designates Tier 1
deadline: As soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the situation
notify: All persons served, by broadcast media, posting, hand delivery, or another method approved in writing by the primacy agency
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the incident interrupted key treatment or off-spec water may have entered distribution. Decision owner: Water Quality Supervisor with the General Manager

deadline: Initiate as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the system learns of the situation; then follow any added requirements from the consultation
notify: State drinking water primacy agency (after-hours contact in the PN SOP)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes with any Tier 1 situation. Recommended as a courtesy call for any confirmed tampering even without a Tier 1 trigger

obligation: Report failure to comply with a drinking water regulation
trigger: The incident causes a violation of a national primary drinking water regulation, including missed required monitoring
deadline: Within 48 hours (unless the part sets a different period)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a violation results (for example missed compliance monitoring while SCADA is down)

trigger: Completion of the initial public notice and any repeat notices
deadline: Within 10 days of completing the public notification requirements, with a representative copy of each type of notice
Keep copies for 3 years after issuance

citation: 42 U.S.C. 300i-1 (tampering, attempt, or threat to tamper with a public water system is a federal crime)
trigger: Evidence that someone interfered or attempted to interfere with the operation of the system
deadline: No statutory reporting deadline. Company rule: notify the FBI as soon as the incident is declared
notify: FBI field office (and IC3 online report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for any confirmed unauthorized control action. Preserve evidence for investigators

citation: Voluntary. No federal mandatory cyber incident reporting rule applied to water systems as of 2026-09-25
deadline: As soon as possible. Company rule: within 24 hours of declaration
notify: CISA (and the water-sector information sharing center once the company joins)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes (voluntary). Reporting to law enforcement or CISA is also a mitigating factor for OFAC if a ransom is ever considered

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered through the water-sector criterion (community water system serving more than 3,300) even though it is SBA-small. Recheck when final

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example customer names with online account credentials if the attacker reached the CIS or business network)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay allowed on written request)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed. An HMI compromise alone does not trigger it; confirm during analysis whether the attacker reached business systems

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Floridians' personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains or processes customer personal information for the company (for example the CIS vendor) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The company (Customer Service and Billing Manager and IT Manager)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information was accessed and some affected customers live outside Florida (for example seasonal residents with out-of-state billing addresses)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. Applies if the HMI incident turns into extortion

deadline: Per policy (as soon as practicable; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring outside vendors)

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
